avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (taken simultaneously)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium binds pamidronate in GI tract, significantly reducing bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; take pamidronate on empty stomach

avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Iron forms chelate complexes with bisphosphonates, reducing absorption of both agents
avoid_supplements.action: Separate by minimum 2 hours; counsel on empty stomach administration

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium chelates pamidronate, reducing oral absorption and bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Administer pamidronate on empty stomach, separated from magnesium by ≥2 hours

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase serum calcium levels; pamidronate lowers calcium, creating opposing effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum calcium and phosphate levels; coordinate supplementation with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase risk of GI irritation and osteonecrosis of the jaw when combined with bisphosphonates
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose; consider gastroprotection; monitor oral health

avoid_foods.name: High-calcium dairy products (taken within 2 hours)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Dietary calcium significantly impairs pamidronate absorption through chelation in GI lumen
avoid_foods.action: Maintain 2-hour separation between pamidronate and dairy intake; administer on empty stomach

caution_foods.name: Iron-rich foods (red meat, fortified cereals)
caution_foods.mechanism: High dietary iron may reduce pamidronate bioavailability if consumed simultaneously
caution_foods.action: Separate meals containing high iron from pamidronate administration by ≥2 hours when possible

monitoring_notes: Pamidronate is primarily renally excreted and does not undergo hepatic metabolism, limiting drug-drug interactions but requiring renal function monitoring. Monitor serum calcium, phosphate, and magnesium levels regularly, particularly in patients with renal impairment or concurrent use of agents affecting electrolytes.
